The bāʾ in بِطَغْواها is like the bāʾ in كتبت بالقلم ("I wrote with the pen"). The word ṭughwā (طغوى) comes from ṭughyān (transgression). In the pattern fa'lā, which derives from a root with a yāʾ, they distinguished the noun from the adjective. In the noun they changed the yāʾ into wāw, but in the adjective they left it unchanged, so they said: imra'a khazyā wa-ṣadyā (امرأة خزيي وصديى). The meaning is: "They denied (the truth) through their transgression (فعلت التكذيب بطغيانها), as you say: 'He wronged me through his audacity against God' (ظلمني بجرأته على الله)." It was also said: "They denied what they were threatened with of its punishment, (the one) of ṭughwā," like His words ﴿So they were destroyed by the Overwhelming Blast﴾ (فَأُهْلِكُوا بِالطَّاغِيَةِ). Al-Ḥasan recited بطغواها with a ḍamma on the ṭāʾ, like al-ḥusnā and al-rujʿā as verbal nouns.

إِذِ انْبَعَثَ is in the accusative, governed by كذبت or by الطغوى.

وأَشْقاها refers to Qudār ibn Sālif. It is permissible that they were a group, and the singular is used because when you make an elative (af'al al-tafḍīl) the comparison is between one and many, and between masculine and feminine, and it would also be permissible to say أشقوها, as you say أفاضلهم.

The pronoun in لَهُمْ may refer to the two most wretched (of them), and the superlative is in wretchedness, because whoever undertakes and carries out the slaughter, his wretchedness is more manifest and more complete.

ناقَةَ اللَّهِ is in the accusative as a warning, like your saying "The lion! The lion!" and "The child! The child!", with the implied verb: "Beware of" or "Take care of" (ذروا أو احذروا) its slaughter (عقرها).

وَسُقْياها: do not keep her from it (فلا تزووها عنها), and do not monopolize it over her (ولا تستأثروا بها عليها).

﴿So they denied him﴾ (فَكَذَّبُوهُ) regarding what he warned them of, the descent of punishment if they did it.

﴿So their Lord brought down upon them a devastation﴾ (فَدَمْدَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ): He let the punishment fall upon them. It comes from the repetition of the phrase "a she-camel that is madmūma" (ناقة مدمومة), meaning when the fat has covered her.

﴿because of their sin﴾ (بِذَنْبِهِمْ): because of their sin. In this there is a great warning about the consequence of sin, so every sinner must take heed and beware.

﴿And He levelled it﴾ (فَسَوَّاها): the pronoun refers to the devastation, meaning: He levelled it over them, so that neither their young nor their old escaped it.

﴿And He does not fear its consequence﴾ (وَلا يَخافُ عُقْباها): that is, its outcome and its sequel, as every punisher among kings fears (the consequence), so that some restraint remains. It is also permissible that the pronoun refers to Thamūd, in the sense: "He levelled them to the ground," or "in their destruction," and "He does not fear the aftermath of their destruction."

In the codices of the people of Medina and Syria it reads فلا يخاف. In the recitation of the Prophet (ﷺ) it reads ولم يخف.

From the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Sūrat al-Shams, it is as if he gave charity of everything that the sun and the moon have risen upon."

[Narrated by al-Tha'labī, al-Wāḥidī and Ibn Mardawayh, with a chain going back to Ubayy ibn Ka'b.]

The pronoun in لَهُمْ may refer to the two most wretched (of them), and the superlative is in wretchedness, because whoever undertakes and carries out the slaughter, his wretchedness is more manifest and more complete.

ناقَةَ اللَّهِ is in the accusative as a warning, like your saying "The lion! The lion!" and "The child! The child!", with the implied verb: "Beware of" or "Take care of" (ذروا أو احذروا) its slaughter (عقرها).

وَسُقْياها: do not keep her from it (فلا تزووها عنها), and do not monopolize it over her (ولا تستأثروا بها عليها).

﴿So they denied him﴾ (فَكَذَّبُوهُ) regarding what he warned them of, the descent of punishment if they did it.

﴿So their Lord brought down upon them a devastation﴾ (فَدَمْدَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ): He let the punishment fall upon them. It comes from the repetition of the phrase "a she-camel that is madmūma" (ناقة مدمومة), meaning when the fat has covered her.

﴿because of their sin﴾ (بِذَنْبِهِمْ): because of their sin. In this there is a great warning about the consequence of sin, so every sinner must take heed and beware.

﴿And He levelled it﴾ (فَسَوَّاها): the pronoun refers to the devastation, meaning: He levelled it over them, so that neither their young nor their old escaped it.

﴿And He does not fear its consequence﴾ (وَلا يَخافُ عُقْباها): that is, its outcome and its sequel, as every punisher among kings fears (the consequence), so that some restraint remains. It is also permissible that the pronoun refers to Thamūd, in the sense: "He levelled them to the ground," or "in their destruction," and "He does not fear the aftermath of their destruction."

In the codices of the people of Medina and Syria it reads فلا يخاف. In the recitation of the Prophet (ﷺ) it reads ولم يخف.

From the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Sūrat al-Shams, it is as if he gave charity of everything that the sun and the moon have risen upon."

[Narrated by al-Tha'labī, al-Wāḥidī and Ibn Mardawayh, with a chain going back to Ubayy ibn Ka'b.]

The bāʾ in بِطَغْواها is like the bāʾ in كتبت بالقلم ("I wrote with the pen"). The word ṭughwā (طغوى) comes from ṭughyān (transgression). In the pattern fa'lā, which derives from a root with a yāʾ, they distinguished the noun from the adjective. In the noun they changed the yāʾ into wāw, but in the adjective they left it unchanged, so they said: imra'a khazyā wa-ṣadyā (امرأة خزيي وصديى). The meaning is: "They denied (the truth) through their transgression (فعلت التكذيب بطغيانها), as you say: 'He wronged me through his audacity against God' (ظلمني بجرأته على الله)." It was also said: "They denied what they were threatened with of its punishment, (the one) of ṭughwā," like His words ﴿So they were destroyed by the Overwhelming Blast﴾ (فَأُهْلِكُوا بِالطَّاغِيَةِ).
